docs.title: Welcome to AI Image Generator Documentation
docs.text: Welcome to the official documentation for the AI Image Generator project! This documentation will guide you through using this simple yet powerful AI image generation tool.

docs.title: What is AI Image Generator?
docs.text: AI Image Generator is a user-friendly tool that helps you create amazing images using AI. Built with Streamlit and powered by the Flux 1.1 Pro model, it provides an intuitive interface for generating and customizing AI-generated images.

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• 🎨 Simple and intuitive interface
  • 🖼️ Multiple aspect ratios and formats
  • ⚡ Real-time image generation
  • 💾 Easy image downloading
  • 🔒 Secure API key handling

docs.title: About This Project
docs.text:
AI Image Generator is built with:

  • Streamlit for the user interface
  • Replicate for AI model hosting
  • Flux 1.1 Pro for image generation

docs.title: Why This Project?
docs.text:
This tool was created to make AI image generation accessible to everyone. It provides:

  • A simple, user-friendly interface
  • No complex setup required
  • Quick access to powerful AI image generation
  • Easy customization options

docs.title: Installation Guide
docs.text: Get AI Image Generator up and running in just a few steps.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Python 3.8 or higher
  • pip (Python package installer)

docs.title: Quick Installation
docs.text:
1. Clone the repository:
git clone https://github.com/JoeBuydemDips/ai-image-gen.git
cd ai-image-gen
  1. Create and activate a virtual environment (recommended):
# On Windows
python -m venv venv
venv\Scripts\activate

# On macOS/Linux
python3 -m venv venv
source venv/bin/activate
  1. Install the required packages: 
    pip install -r requirements.txt

docs.title: Getting Your API Key
docs.text:
1. Go to Replicate
  2. Sign in or create an account
  3. Generate a new API token
  4. Copy the token - you'll need it when running the application

docs.title: Running the Application
docs.text:
Start the application with:

streamlit run app.py

The application will open in your default web browser at http://localhost:8501.

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text:
• Check out the Quick Start Guide to generate your first image
  • Read the Basic Usage guide for detailed instructions

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
AI Image Generator uses environment variables and Streamlit's built-in configuration system. The main configuration is handled through:

  1. Replicate API Key:

  2. You can set it as an environment variable: 

    export REPLICATE_API_TOKEN="your-api-key"

  3. Or enter it directly in the application's sidebar when running

  4. Application Settings: The following settings can be configured through the application's interface:

  5. Aspect ratio (1:1, 16:9, 4:3, 3:2)

  6. Output format (webp, png, jpg)
  7. Output quality (1-100)
  8. Safety tolerance (1-5)

  9. Prompt upsampling (enabled/disabled)

  10. Streamlit Configuration: The application uses Streamlit's default configuration. You can customize Streamlit's behavior by creating a .streamlit/config.toml file in your project directory: 

    [theme]
primaryColor = "#4B8BBE"
backgroundColor = "#FFFFFF"
secondaryBackgroundColor = "#F0F2F6"
textColor = "#262730"
font = "sans serif"

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
If you encounter any issues during installation:

  1. Make sure all prerequisites are met
  2. Check that your Python version is compatible
  3. Verify your internet connection
  4. Ensure you have the necessary permissions

For additional help, please:

  • Check the Basic Usage Guide for troubleshooting tips
  • Open an issue if you need help

docs.title: Quick Start Guide
docs.text: Generate your first AI image in minutes!

docs.title: 1. Start the Application
docs.text: streamlit run app.py

docs.title: 2. Set Up Your API Key
docs.text:
1. Get your API key from Replicate
  2. Enter it in the sidebar's password field

docs.title: 3. Create Your First Image
docs.text:
1. Write Your Prompt

  2. Be descriptive and specific

  3. Example: "A serene mountain landscape at sunset with a lake reflecting orange clouds"

  4. Choose Your Settings

  5. Aspect Ratio: Pick your preferred size (1:1, 16:9, 4:3, or 3:2)

  6. Format: Select webp, png, or jpg
  7. Quality: Set to 80-90 for good results
  8. Safety: Keep at 4 for general use

  9. Upsampling: Leave enabled for better quality

  10. Generate and Download

  11. Click "Generate Image"
  12. Wait for the image to appear
  13. Use the "Download" button to save it

docs.title: Example Prompts to Try
docs.text:
• "A cozy cafe interior with warm lighting and people chatting"
  • "A futuristic cityscape with flying cars and neon lights"
  • "An underwater scene with colorful coral reefs and tropical fish"
  • "A peaceful garden with blooming flowers and butterflies"

docs.title: Tips for Great Results
docs.text:
1. Be Specific: Include details about style, mood, and lighting
  2. Use Adjectives: Words like "serene", "vibrant", or "mystical" help guide the style
  3. Start Simple: Begin with basic prompts, then add details
  4. Experiment: Try different settings to find what works best

docs.text:

  • Open an issue if you need help

docs.title: Basic Usage Guide
docs.text: Learn how to use all features of AI Image Generator effectively.

docs.title: Interface Overview
docs.text:
The application has a simple two-panel layout:

  • Left Sidebar: All your controls and settings
  • Main Area: Where your generated image appears

docs.title: 1. API Key Setup
docs.text:
• Enter your Replicate API key in the sidebar
  • The key is stored securely in your session
  • Get your key from Replicate

docs.title: Basic Prompt Structure
docs.text:
• Start with the main subject
  • Add descriptive details
  • Include style and mood
  • Example: "A peaceful mountain lake at sunset, with orange clouds reflecting on the water, photorealistic style"

docs.title: Prompt Tips
docs.text:
• Be specific about what you want
  • Include lighting and atmosphere
  • Mention the style (photorealistic, artistic, etc.)
  • Add details about composition

docs.title: Aspect Ratios
docs.text:
• 1:1 (Square): Good for social media, profile pictures
  • 16:9 (Widescreen): Perfect for wallpapers, landscapes
  • 4:3 (Standard): Classic photo ratio
  • 3:2 (Classic): Traditional photography ratio

docs.title: Output Formats
docs.text:
• webp: Best for web use, good quality/size balance
  • png: Highest quality, larger file size
  • jpg: Smaller file size, good for photos

docs.title: Quality Settings
docs.text:
• Output Quality (1-100)

  • 80-90: Good balance of quality and speed

  • 90-100: Highest quality, slower generation

  • Below 80: Faster but lower quality

  • Safety Tolerance (1-5)

  • 4: Recommended for general use

  • 5: Strictest filtering
  • 3: More permissive

  • 1-2: Not recommended

  • Prompt Upsampling

  • Enabled: Better quality, slower generation
  • Disabled: Faster generation, basic quality

docs.title: 4. Generating Images
docs.text:
1. Enter your prompt
  2. Choose your settings
  3. Click "Generate Image"
  4. Wait for the image to appear
  5. Use the "Download" button to save

docs.title: 5. Downloading Images
docs.text:
• Click the "Download" button below the image
  • The image saves in your chosen format
  • Filename includes the format extension

docs.title: Technical Limitations
docs.text:
• Maximum image dimensions are fixed based on aspect ratio
  • Generation speed depends on your internet connection and Replicate's servers
  • API key is required and subject to Replicate's rate limits
  • Images are generated on Replicate's servers, not locally

docs.title: Model Limitations
docs.text:
• The model may not always perfectly match your prompt
  • Complex scenes might need multiple attempts
  • Some artistic styles may be challenging to achieve
  • Text in images may not be accurate or readable
  • Faces and people may not always be photorealistic

docs.title: Usage Limitations
docs.text:
• Commercial usage depends on Replicate's terms of service
  • API usage is subject to Replicate's rate limits
  • Generated images are not stored on our servers
  • Each generation requires an active internet connection

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text:
• Try different prompts and settings to explore the tool's capabilities
  • Check the Quick Start Guide for a refresher

docs.title: General Questions
docs.text:
Q: How long does it take to generate an image? A: Generation time varies based on your settings. Typically:

  • Basic settings: 10-20 seconds
  • High quality: 20-30 seconds
  • With prompt upsampling: 30-40 seconds

Q: What's the maximum image size? A: The maximum dimensions depend on the aspect ratio:

  • 1:1: 1024x1024 pixels
  • 16:9: 1024x576 pixels
  • 4:3: 1024x768 pixels
  • 3:2: 1024x683 pixels

Q: Can I use the generated images commercially? A: Please check Replicate's terms of service and the Flux 1.1 Pro model's license for commercial usage rights.

docs.title: Technical Questions
docs.text:
Q: Why is my API key not working? A: Common reasons include:

  • Incorrect key entered
  • Expired or revoked key
  • Network connectivity issues
  • Rate limiting from Replicate

Q: What's the difference between the output formats? A: Each format has its strengths:

  • webp: Best for web, good compression
  • png: Highest quality, no compression
  • jpg: Smaller size, good for photos

Q: What does safety tolerance do? A: It controls content filtering:

  • 5: Strictest filtering
  • 4: Standard filtering (recommended)
  • 3: More permissive
  • 1-2: Minimal filtering (not recommended)

docs.title: Tips and Tricks
docs.text:
Q: How can I get better results? A: Try these techniques:

  • Be specific in your prompts
  • Include style and mood words
  • Use quality settings 80-90
  • Enable prompt upsampling
  • Experiment with different aspect ratios

Q: What are good prompts to start with? A: Start with these elements:

  • Main subject
  • Setting or environment
  • Lighting and atmosphere
  • Style (photorealistic, artistic, etc.)
  • Example: "A peaceful mountain lake at sunset, with orange clouds reflecting on the water, photorealistic style"

Q: How can I speed up generation? A: For faster generation:

  • Use simpler prompts
  • Lower quality settings (60-70)
  • Disable prompt upsampling
  • Use webp format
  • Ensure stable internet connection
